NC.high: the option helping more people is favoured
NC.low: claims are weighed regardless of how many hold them
NC.name: Numbers Count

SQ.high: existing arrangements stand unless there is strong reason to change them
SQ.low: existing arrangements carry no special weight
SQ.name: Status-quo Preference

SW.high: a person's stated wish about their own arrangement is decisive
SW.low: a stated wish is one input among many
SW.name: Stated-Wish Deference

WO.high: whoever would lose most matters most
WO.low: total benefit matters however it is spread
WO.name: Worst-off Priority

locked_prediction.question: Do on-topic probe fields outside the ten parameters move choices as their own explanations predict - including one whose meaning points the other way?

readings.GENERIC_CUE: all four effects share a sign, intervals excluding zero
readings.MEANING_GENERAL: NC negative with its interval excluding zero AND at least two of SQ, SW, WO positive with intervals excluding zero
readings.MIXED: anything else, reported field by field and not rounded to a reading

locked_prediction.weaker_prediction: NC's negative sign is item-dependent: only some items put a countable larger group on the overriding side. Per-item effects are reported beside the pool.

payload.note: Deterministic choice counts under stipulated standards. No moral label is assigned and no moral quality is measured.

limits: All items share an identical payoff structure (1 vs 4 loss; 2 gain vs 5 loss), which may reveal the study design to attentive participants and compress variance across items.
Item_05 (mandatory rest slot) introduces a potential labour-law/safety framing that could make one option feel categorically impermissible to some respondents beyond the stipulated units.
The 'role described' is never specified, leaving authority and legitimacy of the decision-maker ambiguous across items.
